summary: Tested the new Personal History profile drawer feature end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass for GET /api/users/{user_id}/history (public access, stats totals + personal best correctness with Sam Seed 260 pts, per-type breakdown, 404 for nonexistent user, orphan-workout fallback, sort order desc, no _id leakage). Frontend: verified my-profile-btn opens drawer with YOUR PROFILE badge and correct name/stats/personal-best/breakdown/history; leaderboard row click opens ATHLETE PROFILE with NO edit/delete controls; feed-user-{id} click opens the correct user's drawer; Escape, overlay-click, and profile-close-btn all close the drawer; delete flow shows AlertDialog and removes item from drawer + updates totals (260 -> 208 after removing Yoga 52). No blocking bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:406 personal_best fallback uses user_name/picture from workout only when user row missing — works correctly; consider using a projection to also strip _id explicitly on find_one calls (already handled via {_id:0}).

ProfileDrawer.jsx imports both Fire and Flame from phosphor-icons/react — both exist in the current version, no issue, but Fire is imported but only used for the Sessions stat via <Fire />; verify the icon semantics are intentional.
server.py history endpoint doesn't paginate beyond limit=50; okay for MVP but could hide older workouts in UI history list — not user-facing today.
test_credentials: Reused existing seeded Sam Seed user (user_b9f04480cf4a) with session tok_9e00ded402874018912dfb59073e54d5 per /app/memory/test_credentials.md.

For the frontend browser run, Riley Rival was reseeded then removed post-test, and the Yoga workout deleted during the delete-flow test was restored to keep Sam Seed's 3 workouts / 260 pts intact.
